speaker: augustine_phillips
text: The letter in your hand is the tally. The play's letter is in the basket, under the ribbons.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: Then label the basket. I will not sort ribbons while a man waits on a word.

speaker: richard_cowley
text: I have learned the line that answers the letter. I have not learned the paper. Tell me once, and I will keep the once.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The play's letter has no sums on it. The tally has sums. Do not open the tally on the stage.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Third entrance. You come from that door with the letter already in your hand. Not searching. In your hand.

speaker: richard_cowley
text: Third entrance. Already in my hand. I can do that if the right paper is put there before I move.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: I will put it in your hand at the door. I will not carry it out to you in the middle of the yard. I am not a page.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: At the door is right. Again from the entrance. No talk of baskets once you have started.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: When he speaks the word "letter," you are already showing it. Not after the word. On it.

speaker: richard_cowley
text: On the word. I have the line. Now I have the hand as well, if the hand is taught.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: That is the tally. You have done the one thing you were told not to do, and you have done it so the back row could read it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Stop. Turn it over. A Saturday's meat is not this play.

speaker: richard_cowley
text: I am sorry. The ribbon was round this one. I took the ribbon for the sign.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: The sign is the hand that gives it to you, not the ribbon. Pope's hand. At the door. Once more.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: My hand. This paper. No sums. If I give you the wrong one, the fault is mine, and you may say so afterwards.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Good. The fault can have an owner. Again.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Third entrance. The word. The paper. No apology in the middle. Apologies are for this morning, not for two of the clock.

speaker: richard_cowley
text: No apology at two. I will look at Pope's hand. If I am wrong I will turn the paper and go on.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Going on is the rule. Two of the clock. Once it is the right paper, it is only a paper.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: I will keep the tally in my belt, so it cannot become the right paper by lying near it.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Do that. And no music under the letter. The speech is dry. Let it stay dry.

speaker: richard_cowley
text: Dry. I can be dry. I have learned it dry, and I will say it dry.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then we are done with it. Eat before two. The scene does not need a man hurrying the end of it.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: Cold meat in the tiring-house, and the tally in my belt. I can hold both ideas at once.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: I will look at his hand at the half hour. Monday was a peg. Today is a hand. I am not above checking either.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Look once, and then leave it. The afternoon belongs to the play.
